evidence.note: עוֹבָל appears by name alongside Abimael and Sheba.
The closing statement identifies all those listed as sons of Joktan.

article.name: עוֹבָל
article.summary: Obal is a son of Joktan. Genesis lists him immediately before Abimael and Sheba.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for עוֹבָל. Leave the root unassigned because the passage gives no support for the proposed meaning “spotted” or “marked.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:26 introduces Joktan as the father, 10:28 names Obal, and 10:29 calls those listed Joktan’s sons.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 10:28 names Obal alongside Abimael and Sheba, each introduced by וְאֶת. Genesis 10:29 identifies them all as sons of Joktan. The genealogy gives no explanation of the name’s meaning.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun without a prefix or suffix. The preceding וְאֶת is a separate word that marks Obal as another direct object of יָלַד, “fathered,” in Genesis 10:26.
